h: From Woodland Paths to Maritime History
p: New Forest Wildlife Park is a great fit for families who'd rather spend time outdoors than queue for big rides. The site sits in the forest near Ashurst, between Southampton and Lyndhurst, so you're never far from the main roads, but once you're under the trees it feels miles from anywhere. Keeper talks are well worth catching, especially for the otters, and give children the chance to ask the questions they've been saving up. Allow a good few hours and you won't feel hurried.

There's plenty more to tie in nearby. Longdown Activity Farm, close to the wildlife park, is an easy-going farm attraction with animals to meet and feed, ideal for younger children. Lyndhurst, often called the capital of the New Forest, is home to the New Forest Heritage Centre, which tells the story of the forest and its ponies. Further south, the National Motor Museum at Beaulieu has a huge collection of cars, plus the palace house and abbey ruins, and the riverside village of Bucklers Hard is a lovely spot where ships for Nelson's navy were once built.

Head back into Southampton and you can dive into maritime history. SeaCity Museum explores the city's link with the Titanic, which sailed from Southampton in 1912, and the Tudor House and Garden is a timber-framed house packed with centuries of history. Sections of the medieval walls still stand, and the waterfront is great for watching the cruise ships come and go. It's a lovely contrast to a morning spent among the trees and the otters.
